summary: SPHEREx SkyBlink is an interactive web application built with Python and Streamlit that transforms how users explore multi-spectral astrophysical data inspired by NASA’s SPHEREx mission. Adapting the classic astronomical "blink comparator" technique into a modern browser tool, it allows users to rapidly toggle between spectral bands and celestial observations to spot subtle variations, transient phenomena, and hidden cosmic structures. This approach addresses the challenge of making complex astronomical datasets accessible without heavy desktop software, empowering students, researchers, and citizen scientists to easily investigate galaxy formation, interstellar biogenic molecules, and cosmic evolution.
details:
Project Overview & How It Works:SPHEREx SkyBlink is an interactive web application designed to visualize, compare, and analyze astrophysical data inspired by NASA’s SPHEREx mission. Utilizing a "sky-blinking" technique, the platform allows users to rapidly toggle between different spectral bands and celestial observations to easily detect subtle variations, transient phenomena, and hidden cosmic structures.

Intended Impact & Benefits: By simplifying multi-spectral sky exploration, SPHEREx SkyBlink bridges the gap between complex astrophysical datasets and accessible visual analysis. It empowers students, researchers, and citizen scientists to quickly identify anomalies and gain deeper insights into galaxy formation, water and biogenic molecules in interstellar space, and the evolution of the universe.

Tools, Technologies & Software:

  • Programming Language: Python
  • Framework & UI: Streamlit (for building a responsive, interactive web interface)
  • Data Processing & Visualization: Scientific Python libraries for data manipulation, spectral filtering, and dynamic plotting
  • Version Control & Hosting: Git & GitHub

Creativity & Design Considerations: Instead of relying on static data tables or overly complex astronomical software, SPHEREx SkyBlink adapts the classic astronomical "blink comparator" method into a modern, lightweight web tool. Key considerations included minimizing latency during rapid frame switching, ensuring intuitive controls for non-specialists, and maintaining scientific fidelity across spectral views.
